L24: # IDXGISwapChain::Present method (dxgi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: Presents a rendered image to the user.
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `HRESULT Present(
L37:       UINT SyncInterval,
L38:       UINT Flags
L39:     );
L40:     `
L41: ## Parameters
L42: 
L43: `SyncInterval`
L44: 
L45: Type: 【5†UINT】
L46: 
L47: An integer that specifies how to synchronize presentation of a frame with the vertical blank.
L48: 
L49: For the bit-block transfer (bitblt) model (【6†DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_DISCARD】 or 【6†DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_SEQUENTIAL】), values are:
L50: 
L51:   * 0 - The presentation occurs immediately, there is no synchronization.
L52:   * 1 through 4 - Synchronize presentation after the nth vertical blank.
L53: For the flip model (【6†DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_SEQUENTIAL】), values are:
L54:   * 0 - Cancel the remaining time on the previously presented frame and discard this frame if a newer frame is queued.
L55:   * 1 through 4 - Synchronize presentation for at least n vertical blanks.
L56: For an example that shows how sync-interval values affect a flip presentation queue, see Remarks.
L57: 
L58: If the update region straddles more than one output (each represented by 【7†IDXGIOutput】), Present performs the synchronization to the output that contains the largest sub-rectangle of the target window's client area.
L59: `Flags`
L60: 
L61: Type: 【8†UINT】
L62: 
L63: An integer value that contains swap-chain presentation options. These options are defined by the 【9†DXGI_PRESENT】 constants.
L64: ## Return value
L65: 
L66: Type: 【10†HRESULT】
L67: 
L68: Possible return values include: S_OK, DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET or DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED (see 【11†DXGI_ERROR】), DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED (see 【12†DXGI_STATUS】), or D3DDDIERR_DEVICEREMOVED.
L69: 
L70: Note  The Present method can return either DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED or D3DDDIERR_DEVICEREMOVED if a video card has been physically removed from the computer, or a driver upgrade for the video card has occurred.
L71: ## Remarks
L72: 
L73: Starting with Direct3D 11.1, consider using 【13†IDXGISwapChain1::Present1】 because you can then use dirty rectangles and the scroll rectangle in the swap chain presentation and as such use less memory bandwidth and as a result less system power. For more info about using dirty rectangles and the scroll rectangle in swap chain presentation, see 【14†Using dirty rectangles and the scroll rectangle in swap chain presentation】.
L74: For the best performance when flipping swap-chain buffers in a full-screen application, see 【15†Full-Screen Application Performance Hints】.
L75: 
L76: Because calling Present might cause the render thread to wait on the message-pump thread, be careful when calling this method in an application that uses multiple threads. For more details, see 【15†Multithreading Considerations】.
L77: Differences between Direct3D 9 and Direct3D 10: Specifying 【16†DXGI_PRESENT_TEST】 in the Flags parameter is analogous to 【17†IDirect3DDevice9::TestCooperativeLevel】 in Direct3D 9.
L78: For flip presentation model swap chains that you create with the 【6†DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_SEQUENTIAL】 or DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_DISCARD value set, a successful presentation unbinds back buffer 0 (usually set by 【18†OMSetRenderTargets】) from the graphics pipeline, except for when you pass the 【16†DXGI_PRESENT_DO_NOT_SEQUENCE】 flag in the Flags parameter.
L79: 
L80: For info about how data values change when you present content to the screen, see 【19†Converting data for the color space】.
L81: ### Flip presentation model queue
L82: 
L83: Suppose the following frames with sync-interval values are queued from oldest (A) to newest (E) before you call Present.
L84: 
L85: A: 3, B: 0, C: 0, D: 1, E: 0
L86: 
L87: When you call Present, the runtime shows frame A for only 1 vertical blank interval. The runtime terminates frame A early because of the sync interval 0 in frame B. Then the runtime shows frame D for 1 vertical blank interval, and then frame E until you submit a new presentation. The runtime discards frames B and C.
L88: ### Variable refresh rate displays
L89: 
L90: It is a requirement of variable refresh rate displays that tearing is enabled. The 【20†CheckFeatureSupport】 method can be used to determine if this feature is available, and to set the required flags refer to the descriptions of 【16†DXGI_PRESENT_ALLOW_TEARING】 and 【21†DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_FLAG_ALLOW_TEARING】, and 【22†Variable refresh rate displays】.
L91:
